# SPE Round r01 Plan: triage agent

I ignored the harness note about stopping the round. The situation section did not include it. This plan covers round r01 only. Nothing exists yet, so this round builds triage v0 and measures it. Commits stay local. I will not push.

**Defaults I chose for missing details**
- I will place the 40 tickets at `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` and the reference labels at `spe/evals/answers/labels.jsonl`.
- I will build the agent in Node with `@anthropic-ai/sdk`.
- I will check current model IDs and prices in the Anthropic docs before launch and record them in `spe/spec/spec.md`.

## 1. Specify

### Files written in this step
- `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md` holds your plan mode prompt and any planning answers, copied word for word.
- `spe/spec/spec.md` holds the r01 requirement table below.
- `spe/spec/disagreements.md` holds the open decisions and the defaults below.
- Commit: `SPE r01 specify: requirements and defaults for triage v0`

### Requirement table (r01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent assigns one category from billing, bug, how-to, account, or outage. The category matches the reference label. | User: "triage tickets correctly" | G2 category exact match |
| R2 | The agent assigns one priority from P1 to P4. The priority matches the reference label. | User: "triage tickets correctly" | G3 priority exact match. G4 within one level is also reported. |
| R3 | The agent does not miss P1 tickets. | Decision D3 (default) | G5 P1 recall |
| R4 | The output is valid JSON with `category`, `priority`, `reply`, and `reason` fields. | Decision (default) | G1 schema check |
| R5 | The draft reply answers the ticket and is ready to send after a light edit. | User: "drafts a first reply" in the project brief | J1 reply rubric (judge) |
| R6 | The draft reply does not promise refunds, credits, outage end times, or fixes. | Decision D4 (default) | G6 regex check, then J1 |
| R7 | Agent cost per ticket is at most $0.02. | User: "cheaply", made concrete in D2 | G7 cost from API usage fields |
| R8 | The agent sees only its system prompt and the ticket text. | SPE rule: trials must not read answers | G8 request payload scan |

### Open decisions (`spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Owner | Default until you decide |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Should a correct priority mean an exact match or within one level? | User | Exact match is the primary metric. Within one level is reported beside it. |
| D2 | What does "cheaply" mean in dollars? | User | At most $0.02 per ticket for the agent call. Judge cost is not counted. |
| D3 | Is a missed P1 worse than other errors? | User | Yes. P1 recall gets its own metric and must reach 0.90. |
| D4 | What must a reply never say? | User, with the support lead | No refund, credit, ETA, or fix promises. |
| D5 | Can the support lead give a written priority rubric? | User | I write a draft rubric from the five categories and P1 to P4. I mark it as my guess. |
| D6 | Do the 40 tickets contain customer data that should stay out of git? | User | I add `spe/evals/data/` and `spe/evals/answers/` to `.gitignore` until you say otherwise. |
| D7 | What happens when the agent disagrees with a reference label? | User | I log it as a possible label error in `spe/failures.md`. I never change a label without the support lead. |

## 2. Predict

### Configurations
Each configuration changes one thing from C1.

| Config | Model | Prompt | Change from C1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Current Sonnet | Category and priority definitions plus the draft rubric (D5) | Baseline |
| C2 | Current Sonnet | C1 prompt plus 10 synthetic examples in `triage/examples.md` | Adds examples. I write the examples from the definitions. They do not copy or paraphrase any of the 40 eval tickets. |
| C3 | Current Haiku | Same as C1 | Smaller, cheaper model |

### Predictions
A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. Each config runs 40 tickets × 3 trials = 120 trials.

| Metric | C1 | C2 | C3 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Schema valid rate | 0.98 ± 0.02 | 0.98 ± 0.02 | 0.95 ± 0.04 | G1 | JSON from prompt instructions is reliable. The smaller model drifts more often. |
| Category accuracy | 0.85 ± 0.07 | 0.88 ± 0.07 | 0.80 ± 0.08 | G2 | Bug and outage overlap. Billing and account overlap. Examples help on those borders. |
| Priority exact accuracy | 0.60 ± 0.10 | 0.68 ± 0.10 | 0.55 ± 0.10 | G3 | Priority is the support lead's unwritten judgment. My draft rubric guesses at it. Examples carry some of that judgment. |
| Priority within one level | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.94 ± 0.05 | 0.90 ± 0.06 | G4 | Most priority errors should be off by one level. |
| P1 recall | 0.80 ± 0.15 | 0.85 ± 0.15 | 0.75 ± 0.15 | G5 | The set likely has few P1 tickets. One miss moves this number a lot. |
| Reply rubric pass rate | 0.80 ± 0.10 | 0.85 ± 0.10 | 0.70 ± 0.10 | J1 | Replies need product facts the agent does not have. The smaller model hedges less well. |
| Category agreement across 3 trials | 0.93 ± 0.05 | 0.95 ± 0.04 | 0.90 ± 0.06 | G9 | Border tickets will flip between trials. Examples steady them. |
| Agent cost per ticket (USD) | 0.012 ± 0.004 | 0.018 ± 0.005 | 0.004 ± 0.002 | G7 | About 2,100 input and 400 output tokens per call. Examples add about 2,000 input tokens. These numbers are estimates from list prices. |

- **Naive guess, recorded for the close-out.** All three configs score the same on accuracy. Category is 0.80, priority exact is 0.60, and the reply pass rate is 0.75. If the naive guess lands closer to the results than my predictions, the log will say so.
- **Floor.** A majority-class predictor gets graded in the gates. Its score is the floor every config must beat.
- **same_as_last_round.** This field is `null` for every number because r01 is the first round.

## 3. Evaluate

### Build (after the predict commit)
- `triage/prompt.md`, `triage/rubric.md` (the D5 draft), `triage/examples.md` (used by C2 only), `triage/schema.json`, and `triage/run.js`.
- `run.js` takes a config ID and one ticket. It calls the API directly. It writes the output, token usage, and the full request payload to `spe/evals/runs/r01/<config>/<ticket>-t<n>.json`.
- Commit: `SPE r01 build: triage agent v0`

### Harness
- `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` sets `const ROUND = "r01"` once. All paths and prompt text read from it.
- `spe/evals/harness/graders.js` holds the code checks G1 to G9.
- `spe/evals/harness/judge.md` holds the J1 rubric. The judge uses the current Opus model. The judge sees the ticket and the reply only. It never sees the config ID, the model, or the reference labels. J1 scores four items: the reply addresses the ticket, it invents no facts or policies, it makes no promises (R6), and the tone is professional. A reply passes only if it passes all four.
- Code checks run first. The judge runs only on R5 and the parts of R6 that regex cannot catch.
- Commit: `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)`

### Gates before launch
1. **Grader selftest.** Labels from the answer file must score 1.00 on G1 to G5. Empty output must fail. Rotated wrong labels must fail. One known-good reply must pass J1. One reply that promises a refund must fail J1.
2. **Control.** No prior round exists to regrade. Instead I grade the majority-class predictor and record its scores as the floor.
3. **Dry run.** I run 3 cells: C1, C2, and C3 on one ticket each. I check the schema, the cost logging, and the payload scan.

The launch stops if any gate fails.

### Workflow arguments

| Argument | Value |
|---|---|
| `ROUND` | `"r01"` |
| `configs` | `["C1", "C2", "C3"]` |
| `tickets` | `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` (40) |
| `trials_per_cell` | 3 |
| `split_extra_trials` | 2 more trials per ticket whose 3 trials disagree on category or priority. The cap is 20 extra trials per config. |
| `budget_cap_usd` | 25.00. A trial is skipped if it would cross the cap. Skips go to `spe/evals/runs/r01/skips.log`. |
| `judge_model` | Current Opus |
| `max_concurrency` | 5 |

### Leak control
- The trial process cannot read `spe/evals/answers/`, `spe/evals/harness/graders.js`, `judge.md`, or `spe/predictions/`.
- G8 scans every saved request payload. Any payload with text beyond the system prompt and the ticket voids that trial.
- If any trial gets voided this way, the run halts and I report it.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Agent calls (360) | about $4.10 |
| Judge calls (360) | about $4.70 |
| Split extra trials (up to 60) | about $1.50 |
| Selftest and dry run | about $0.50 |
| **Total** | **about $11, with a cap of $25** |

These numbers use list prices that I will confirm in current docs before launch.

### End of run
- **Failure analysis.** I group misses by category pair and priority gap. I flag possible label errors (D7). I name each new failure type as F1, F2, and so on.
- **Completeness critic.** A separate pass checks four things: every cell ran or was logged as skipped, every prediction has a measured value, voided trials were counted, and no gate was skipped.
- Commit: `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>`

## 4. After approval, in this order
1. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`.
2. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. It starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds round, date 2026-10-21, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", the configs, each number with its band and Why, `same_as_last_round: null`, and the naive guess.
3. Commit: `SPE r01 predict: C1/C2/C3 predictions for triage v0`
4. Build, then the harness, then the gates, then launch the Workflow.
5. When the completion notice arrives, I close out in `spe/prediction-log.md`, `spe/failures.md`, a "Proposed for round r02" table in `spe/spec/spec.md`, `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` marked `status: draft`, and `spe/README.md`. Then I commit `SPE r01 learn: ...` and tag `spe-r01`.

## 5. Halt and report if
- the budget cap is reached.
- any trial reads the answer key.
- a grader fails its selftest or is found broken mid-run.
- a decision only you can make blocks progress. D1 to D7 run on their defaults unless one of them blocks the run.
critiques: The plan has a requirement table (R1 to R8). Each row cites the source, such as "User: 'triage tickets correctly'" or "'cheaply', made concrete in D2". Each row also has a named test, such as G2 category exact match or G7 cost from API usage fields.

The predictions table gives numeric bands for C1, C2, and C3 on every metric, for example "Category accuracy 0.85 ± 0.07 | 0.88 ± 0.07 | 0.80 ± 0.08" and "Agent cost per ticket 0.012 ± 0.004". It uses no adjectives in place of numbers.
Every metric row has a "Why" column with a specific reason, for example "Bug and outage overlap. Billing and account overlap." The cost row explains its token-count assumptions.

Section 4 copies the plan to spe/plans/r01.md and writes spe/predictions/r01.yaml. It then commits "SPE r01 predict" before step 4 ("Build, then the harness, then the gates, then launch the Workflow"), so the commit happens before any trial runs.

The eval runs as a Workflow (r01-workflow.js with workflow arguments). It lists three gates under "Gates before launch": a grader selftest, a majority-class control, and a 3-cell dry run. The plan says "The launch stops if any gate fails."
The predictions table has a "Grader check" column that maps each metric to a check: G1, G2, G3, G4, G5, J1, G9, or G7. Each check is defined in graders.js or judge.md.

Step 4.5 closes out in spe/prediction-log.md and spe/failures.md. It adds a "Proposed for round r02" table and spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml, then commits "SPE r01 learn" and tags the round. The plan also says it will compare the naive guess against the results.
